children: Asian spot liquefied natural gas prices hit a new 45-month high this week as disruptions caused by the conflict in the Middle East and strong South Asia demand ahead of winter continued to support prices and intensify competition with Europe.

The average price for November delivery into north-east Asia (LNG-AS) was estimated at $27.00 per million British thermal units (mmBtu), the highest since December 30, 2022 and up from $26.00/mmBtu last week.

"Spot global gas prices have traded at high levels over the last week as Europe and Asia continue to compete for cargoes ahead of the winter, with European storage remaining low for the time of year," said Alex Froley, senior LNG analyst at data intelligence firm ICIS.

"The recent surge in prices comes as the market realizes there will likely be no solution before the winter season begins. This could drive up business and household energy bills, which in time will feed into a wider economic impact on inflation and interest rates over coming months," he added.
South Asian demand has held firm, with Bangladesh, India and Thailand consistently issuing spot tenders, said Martin Senior, head of LNG pricing at Argus.
Weather is probably the biggest demand-side swing factor, said Tom Purdie, lead LNG analyst at consultancy Energy Aspects.

"El Nino conditions generally point towards a warmer winter, but also raise the risk of a late-winter polar-vortex disruption. The difficult scenario would be cold weather hitting Europe and Asia together, simultaneously raising European heating demand and Asian LNG buying," he said.
A meaningful supply recovery via the Strait of Hormuz still requires the underlying security situation to ease.

"That leaves Europe and Asia competing for the same Atlantic LNG. Asian buyers have already been willing to pay into the high-$20s/mmBtu, although affordability is increasingly becoming a constraint. The key question this winter is how much Asian demand is destroyed before enough Atlantic cargoes are released back towards Europe," Purdie said.

S&P Global Energy assessed its daily Northwest Europe LNG price benchmark for cargoes delivered in October on an ex-ship basis at $25.395/mmBtu on Thursday, a $0.435/mmBtu discount to the front-month price at the Dutch TTF gas hub.

"The physical LNG market remained comparatively supported by ongoing concerns over Europe's storage position and the need to secure winter supply. European storage levels are around 68.5% full, but remain significantly below historical averages and continue to underpin winter risk premiums," said Aly Blakeway, head of Atlantic LNG at S&P Global Energy.
Argus assessed the price at $25.360/mmBtu, while Spark Commodities assessed it at $25.292/mmBtu.
In LNG freight, Atlantic rates rose to $24,500/day. Pacific rates steadied at $26,750/day, said Spark Commodities analyst Edward Armitage.

US Gulf Coast prompt cargoes are currently priced at $24.178/mmBtu. The U.S. front-month arbitrage to north-east Asia via the Cape of Good Hope continues to point to Europe, while the arbitrage via Panama remains open to Asia, Armitage said.
